answer:
Assume small-deformation linear-elastic solid mechanics.
Assume the shaft is straight, prismatic, and solid circular with radius c and shear modulus G, or piecewise-constant G.
Assume the loads are applied as concentrated torques at discrete cross-sections.
Neglect distributed torque, bending moment, axial force, body forces, and transverse shear force.
Use Saint-Venant torsion so that plane sections remain plane and radii remain straight.
Let x be the axial coordinate and let T(x) be the internal torque at a cross-section.
Equilibrium requires T(x) to be the algebraic sum of all torques applied to one side of the section, with the right-hand-rule sign convention.
The polar second moment of area of the solid circular cross-section is J = π c^4 / 2.
The torsional shear stress at radius r is τ(x,r) = T(x) r / J.
The maximum torsional shear stress occurs at the outer surface and is τ_max(x) = T(x) c / J.
The shear strain is γ(x,r) = τ(x,r) / G = T(x) r / (G J).
The rate of twist is dφ/dx = T(x) / (G J).
For multiple torque locations, divide the shaft into segments between adjacent torque application points and supports.
For any segment i with constant internal torque T_i, length L_i, and torsional rigidity G_i J_i, the relative angle of twist is Δφ_i = T_i L_i / (G_i J_i).
The total relative angle of twist between two cross-sections is φ_B - φ_A = Σ_i T_i L_i / (G_i J_i).
If the shaft is statically indeterminate, enforce compatibility by setting the total twist across redundant segments equal to zero while satisfying torque equilibrium.
The primary response quantities are the internal torque distribution T(x), the shear stress distribution τ(x,r), the shear strain distribution γ(x,r), the maximum shear stress, and the angle-of-twist distribution φ(x).
If the phrase shear loading instead means a transverse shear force V(x), use the additional transverse shear stress formula τ_V(x,y) = 4 V(x) (c^2 - y^2) / (3 π c^4), where y is measured from the neutral axis, and combine it vectorially with the torsional shear stress.
